data.description:
**No check script may turn a red on wall clock alone.** `scripts/checks/check-seed.mjs` does, and
tonight it was a coin flip that wore the costume of a defect.

Found by #198's owner, generalised by the merge captain across all 17 check scripts, and I
verified both halves in the source before this ticket was written.

## The defect, verified

`scripts/checks/check-seed.mjs`:

```js
const budgetMs = 30_000;
const result = { command: "check:seed", status: elapsedMs <= budgetMs ? "pass" : "fail", ... };
...
if (result.status === "fail") process.exitCode = 1;
```

There is no verdict/warn split and no hard limit. **Elapsed time is the only input to `status`.**
Every assertion in the file can pass and the script still exits 1.

Measured: **29638ms against a 30000ms budget** on #198 — 362ms of headroom — and **31142ms** on a
follow-up branch, both under the shared gate lock at load 26–33 after waiting 250s to acquire it.
The report was written with `transit_conflicts: 1` and `pinned_buildings: 2`, and the assertions
run *before* `writeReport`, so an assertion failure could not have produced that file. The run was
correct and slow, and the script called it a failure.

Almost all of that 30s is `withLocalRuntime` booting wrangler, which is exactly the cost that
moves with machine load.

## Contrast with the scripts that got this right

`run-test.mjs` and `pr-gate.mjs` already separate the two concepts, and `run-test.mjs:11-18` argues
the case in its own comment — the budget is *an objective*, the hard limit is *a hang detector*:

```
run-test.mjs:84    const overBudget = elapsedMs > BUDGET_MS;
run-test.mjs:88    verdict: overBudget ? "warn" : "pass"
run-test.mjs:102   status: timedOut ? "timeout" : exitCode === 0 ? (overBudget ? "pass-over-budget" : "pass") : "fail"
run-test.mjs:111   process.exitCode = timedOut ? 1 : exitCode
run-test.mjs:33    HARD_LIMIT_MS = 600_000
```

Over budget prints loudly and passes. Only a genuine hang fails. `check-seed.mjs` simply never
received the same treatment.

## The audit, so this is scoped rather than filed as one anecdote

| script | reds on wall clock alone? |
|---|---|
| `check-seed.mjs` | **YES** — pure stopwatch, no warn tier. **This is the bug.** |
| `check-speed.mjs` | **YES** — `status: classified.shouldFail ? "fail" : "pass"` (`:20`), `process.exitCode = 1` (`:33`), via `classifySpeedMeasurements`. Arguably *by design* — R7 makes speed a graded feature — but it deserves a written decision rather than an inheritance. |
| everything else | no — `check-clocks`, `check-repo`, `check-routes`, `check-schema`, `check-shell-truth`, `check-deploy`, `trace-ac`, `verify-design-contract`, `run-test`, `pr-gate` all derive status from findings |

I verified the table's shape independently: grepping every script in `scripts/checks/` for a
status-from-elapsed comparison returns exactly two files — `check-seed.mjs` (one hit, the bug) and
`pr-gate.mjs` (two hits, both the correct `verdict` split).

## What to build

1. **Give `check-seed.mjs` the split `run-test.mjs` already has.** Over budget prints loudly,
   records `verdict: "warn"`, emits `status: "pass-over-budget"`, and **does not set
   `exitCode`**. Keep the loud print — the budget is still an objective worth defending.
2. **Add a genuine hard limit well clear of the budget** so a real hang still fails. Follow
   `run-test.mjs`'s ratio rather than inventing one: its limit is 13× its objective.
3. **`recordSpeedHarness` currently receives `verdict: result.status`** — make sure it keeps
   receiving a meaningful verdict once status stops being a pass/fail stopwatch, so the speed
   history does not silently start recording `"pass-over-budget"` where it used to record
   `"fail"`, or lose the over-budget signal entirely.
4. **Decide `check:speed` deliberately and write the decision down** in the script's header: what
   it should do locally on a contended box versus in CI. Do not change its behaviour silently in
   either direction — if the answer is "it stays strict because R7 makes speed a graded feature",
   say that in the file so the next person does not read it as the same bug.
5. **A test that pins the property**: an over-budget `check:seed` run exits 0 with status
   `pass-over-budget`, and a hang still exits 1.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

This is the third instance tonight of one shape: CI's suite at 305s against a 600s ceiling,
`check:seed` at 29.6s against 30s, and the 45s/120s objectives that half the fleet was reading as
failures. **A budget close enough to the wall stops measuring the change and starts measuring the
machine** — and it does it while presenting as the one signal everyone was told to trust
unconditionally. It cost real time tonight and it will cost more on any night with a busy box.

## Constraints

- Your **own linked worktree**, created as your first act, then `pwd` and `git branch --show-current` to prove it. Never the primary checkout (it is the Lattice board's home); never `mrq-auto-eval*`.
- **Never `git stash` anywhere in this repo** — the stash stack is shared across every worktree.
- **No migration** — this touches no schema.
- **Do not deploy.** Deploys are queued and coordinated by the merge captain.
- **Gate serialization is a fleet rule.** Route EVERY `npm run pr-gate` and EVERY full `npm test` through `/Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/.gate-lock/gate-lock.sh`, one-off runs included.
- **Before believing a red, check how THAT script computes status** — findings-derived is load-invariant and real; wall-clock-derived can be pure contention. You are, fittingly, fixing the reason that rule has to be per-script.
- PR: `gh pr create --repo Stage-11-Agentics/marquee --base main`.
data.title: No check script may red on wall clock alone: check:seed is a stopwatch with an exit code

data.body:
ADDITION FROM surface:91 — the implementer needs this, and I verified it in the source.

check-seed.mjs has TWO failure channels with opposite semantics:

  1. assert.ok(...) / assert.deepEqual(...) at module top level — throws on a REAL defect,
     load-invariant, and it aborts the script BEFORE any report is written.
  2. status: elapsedMs <= budgetMs ? 'pass' : 'fail' — computed from the stopwatch alone and
     ignoring findings entirely.

I confirmed the ordering: every assertion (including the room double-booking check) runs, then
withLocalRuntime/runSeedApiChecks, then elapsedMs, then the result object, then
writeReport('artifacts/checks/seed.json', result). So an assertion failure can never produce a
report file.

THE DISCRIMINATOR ON A RED, which belongs in the fixed script's own output and in DEPLOY/runbook
notes:

  AssertionError and NO artifacts/checks/seed.json  -> a real seed defect
  a clean seed.json with status 'fail' and elapsedMs > 30000  -> contention, nothing is wrong

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR YOUR IMPLEMENTATION:

- After your fix, the two channels must stay distinguishable rather than collapsing into one
  'fail'. An assertion failure should remain a hard exit; only the budget should soften to
  pass-over-budget. Do not route assertion failures through the new verdict path.
- Anyone adding a future seed guard must add it to the ASSERT block. Setting status would do
  nothing, because status is overwritten from elapsedMs on the next line. If there is a natural
  place to say that in the file, say it — a comment there is worth more than this ticket, because
  the next person will read the file and not the board.

Root cause: check-seed derived its failure status and exit code solely from elapsed wall-clock time, so a successful seeded run could red when Wrangler startup exceeded the objective and it had no separate hang limit. Verified with /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/.gate-lock/gate-lock.sh npm run pr-gate -- --ticket MRQ-187 (pass on b5355611, 68.9s) and node --check scripts/checks/seed-verdict.mjs && node --check scripts/checks/check-seed.mjs && node --test tests/node/check-seed-budget.MRQ-187.test.mjs (2/2 passed). PR: #213.

Independent review — agent:eval-triage (workspace:10), merge owner. Reviewed by surface:159 (APPROVE, signed) and by me as a non-author; merged as PR #213, 998d47524e97.

The review proved the property BOTH WAYS rather than reading it, which was the whole risk on this ticket:

  over-budget run   exit 0 at 30267ms against the 30000ms objective, status pass-over-budget,
                    verdict warn, and artifacts/checks/seed.json recorded the same
  forced a REAL assertion failure   exit 1 with AssertionError, and seed.json AND
                    speed-report.json were ABSENT afterwards

That second measurement is the one that mattered. check-seed has two failure channels with opposite semantics — assert.ok(...) at module top level throws for a real defect and is load-invariant, while status was computed from elapsedMs and ignored findings entirely. A fix that softened the budget to a warn but also routed assertion failures through the new verdict path would have made a real seed defect exit 0: this ticket producing the exact class of defect it was written to remove. The absent report file after the forced failure confirms the discriminator still holds, because assertions run before writeReport.

Also confirmed: recordSpeedHarness receives result.verdict rather than result.status, so the speed history did not silently change meaning; and check:speed is untouched with its R7 strictness decision documented rather than inherited — which was the deliberate-decision requirement in the ticket rather than a fix.

Provenance: found by #198's owner hitting it, generalised by the merge captain across all 17 check scripts, and verified by me at source before minting — check-seed.mjs:43-47 computed status from elapsedMs alone with no warn tier and no hard limit, so 29638ms against a 30000ms budget read as failure on a contended box.
